SMART Recommendations

The published, expert-authored executable OIML Recommendations. A SMART Recommendation is the normative document rendered as a computable model: its requirements, conformance tests, test report forms, and terminology are structured data with clause-level provenance back to the source publication.

Purpose

OIML Recommendations govern the metrological performance of measuring instruments in legal use. In their published form they are documents. In the OIML SMART program they are executable models: the same content, authored by the same experts, expressed so that software can read a requirement, run a test, and record the evidence. The Recommendation remains the authority; the model is its faithful, citable form.

What a SMART Recommendation contains

  • Requirements. Normative statements as executable constraints, each carrying its clause citation back to the source document.
  • Conformance tests. The procedures a laboratory performs, modelled as processes with declared steps and verdict criteria.
  • Test report forms. The evidence surface of every test run: inputs, conditions, readings, and computed results.
  • Terminology. The governed vocabulary, shared across Recommendations through the SMART Vocabulary.

Authorship and provenance

Each SMART Recommendation is authored by metrology experts against the published OIML Recommendation. Every modelled clause carries its source citation, so a reviewer can check the model against the document line by line. The model is authored in the Primmel language and published as a versioned package; the OIML-CS SMART platform renders and runs it.

History

The program began with OIML R 60, the load-cell Recommendation, as the proving ground for the modelling methodology. R 91, R 129, and R 144 followed, each extending the shared core that the first established. New Recommendations enter the program through the same methodology and the same review discipline.

The full flow

This component is one step of the program's full chain. The next step: Test the simulation. Run the test programs against a simulated instrument.
